 Milwaukee tests election equipment ahead of Election Day
 BY 
 Alex Loroff
 Wisconsin 
 PUBLISHED 2:45 PM ET Oct. 24, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 2:45 PM EDT Oct. 24, 2026 
 SHARE 
 MILWAUKEE — Milwaukee election officials are preparing for what is expected to be a busy Election Day on Nov. 3, holding a public test of ballot-counting equipment Saturday as the city works to maintain trust in the process.
 Public testing of election equipment is standard procedure before elections in Wisconsin. Milwaukee Election Commission Director Paulina Gutierrez showed the machines that will count ballots on Election Day as members of the public watched the process.
 “We may see jams early, but then as it starts processing those thousands and thousands of ballots, it gets in the swing of things,” Gutierrez said.
 Among those attending the test were Ben Ginsberg and Bob Bauer, co-chairs of a national organization called Pillars of the Community.
 “Pillars of the Community is very active in seven states, they’re contentious battleground states where election-related issues have been raised before,” Bauer said.
 Ginsberg said the group uses experience from both sides of the political spectrum to help build public confidence in elections.
 “States have different ways of running their elections, and so as we go around the country we get to see those different ways,” Ginsberg said. “Truth is, all of them are reliable.”
 Both Ginsberg and Bauer said they came away from Saturday’s test without doubts that the election will run smoothly in Milwaukee.
 Gutierrez said the city is also looking for additional poll workers to help on Election Day.
 “People sometimes cancel at the last minute, it’s always really hard, it’s a long day, some people just want to do partial shifts,” Gutierrez said. “We want that buffer so in the event it’s busy we’ve got enough staff.”
 The preparations come as Milwaukee faces added attention after three election-related issues since 2024, including during the August primary.
 Gutierrez said the people involved in administering the election are focused on making sure ballots are counted accurately and efficiently.
 “The poll workers, the observers, attorneys, chief inspectors, absentee ballot board of canvassers, everybody is watching this process to ensure that it is safe, secure and fair,” she said.
